intro.value: Seven hills, yellow trams and custard tarts still warm from the oven. Lisbon combines a relaxed Atlantic pace with some of the best viewpoints in Europe.
Gaudí’s architecture, a city beach and tapas until late. Barcelona is a city break and a seaside holiday in one.
Explore the canal ring by boat or by bike, then spend an afternoon with Rembrandt and Van Gogh in the museum quarter.
Colourful harbour fronts, new Nordic cooking and a city that is built for cycling. Copenhagen is at its best on long summer evenings.
Cross Charles Bridge at sunrise, wander through the Old Town and end the day in a traditional beer hall.
Imperial palaces, coffee houses and world-class music. Vienna rewards slow mornings and evenings at the opera.
One of Europe’s largest medieval market squares, the Wawel castle and the lively Kazimierz district.
Walk the city walls above the Adriatic and take a boat to the islands. Come early in the season to avoid the crowds.
A castle on a volcanic rock, cobbled closes and the largest arts festival in the world every August.
Two thousand years of history on every corner, from the Colosseum to the Trevi Fountain, with the best gelato along the way.
A capital spread over fourteen islands, with design shops, archipelago ferries and nights that hardly get dark in summer.
A medieval old town on the Baltic Sea and one of the most digital societies in Europe.

description.value: Bologna is called “la grassa”, the fat one, for good reason. Watch the sfogline fold tortellini by hand and taste mortadella where it was invented.
The capital of French gastronomy. Visit the Halles Paul Bocuse and have lunch in a traditional bouchon lyonnais.
Hop from bar to bar in the old town, where every counter is covered with pintxos and every bar has its own speciality.
Chocolate makers, a proper paper cone of frites and a Belgian beer to finish. Brussels is a city for the sweet tooth.
The birthplace of pizza, fried street food and the strongest espresso in Italy, all in the lively Spanish Quarter.
A sandwich with a reputation, followed by a port wine tasting in one of the cellars across the river in Vila Nova de Gaia.
